Israel Avenged of Her Foes, and Restored, First to Inward Holiness, Then to Outward Prosperity.</title> <div sID="gen21215" type="x-p"/> The distinction between Israel and the heathen (as Edom) is: Israel has a covenant relation to God ensuring restoration after chastisement, so that the heathen's hope of getting possession of the elect people's inheritance must fail, and they themselves be made desolate (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.1-Ezek.36.15">Eze 36:1-15</reference>). The reason for the chastisement of Israel was Israel's sin and profanation of God's name (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.16-Ezek.36.21">Eze 36:16-21</reference>). God has good in store for Israel, for His own name's sake, to revive His people; first, by a spiritual renewal of their hearts, and, next, by an external restoration to prosperity (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.22-Ezek.36.33">Eze 36:22-33</reference>). The result is that the heathen shall be impressed with the power and goodness of God manifested so palpably towards the restored people (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.34-Ezek.36.38">Eze 36:34-38</reference>).<div eID="gen21215" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21216" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11713"/><hi type="bold">1-2. mountains of Israel--</hi>in contrast to "Mount Seir" of the previous prophecy. They are here personified; Israel's elevation is moral, not merely physical, as Edom's. Her hills are "the everlasting hills" of Jacob's prophecy (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.26">Ge 49:26</reference>). "The enemy" (Edom, the singled-out representative of all God's foes), with a shout of exultation, "Aha!" had claimed, as the nearest kinsman of Israel (the brother of their father Esau), his vacated inheritance; as much as to say, the so-called "everlasting" inheritance of Israel and of the "hills," which typified the unmoved perpetuity of it (<reference osisRef="Ps.125.1">Psa 125:1</reference>, 2), has come to an end, in spite of the promise of God, and has become "ours" (compare <reference osisRef="Deut.32.13">De 32:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.33.15">33:15</reference>). <div eID="gen21216" type="x-p"/>

Thou land devourest up men--</hi>alluding to the words of the spies (<reference osisRef="Num.13.32">Nu 13:32</reference>). The land personified is represented as doing that which was done in it. Like an unnatural mother it devoured, that is, it was the grave of its people; of the Canaanites, its former possessors, through mutual wars, and finally by the sword of Israel; and now, of the Jews, through internal and external ills; for example, wars, famine (to which <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.30">Eze 36:30</reference>, "reproach of famine among the heathen," implies the allusion here is). <div eID="gen21232" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11732"/><div sID="gen21244" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11732"/>25. The external restoration must be preceded by an internal one. The change in their condition must not be superficial, but must be based on a radical renewal of the heart. Then the heathen, understanding from the regenerated lives of God's people how holy God is, would perceive Israel's past troubles to have been only the necessary vindications of His righteousness. Thus God's name would be "sanctified" before the heathen, and God's people be prepared for outward blessings.<div eID="gen21244" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21245" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sprinkle ... water--</hi>phraseology taken from the law; namely, the water mixed with the ashes of a heifer sprinkled with a hyssop on the unclean (<reference osisRef="Num.19.9-Num.19.18">Nu 19:9-18</reference>); the thing signified being the cleansing blood of Christ sprinkled on the conscience and heart (<reference osisRef="Heb.9.13">He 9:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.9.14">14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.10.22">10:22</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Jer.33.8">Jr 33:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.5.26">Ep 5:26</reference>).<div eID="gen21245" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21246" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from all your idols--</hi>Literal idolatry has ceased among the Jews ever since the captivity; so far, the prophecy has been already fulfilled; but "cleansing from all their idols," for example, covetousness, prejudices against Jesus of Nazareth, is yet future. <div eID="gen21246" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11739"/><div sID="gen21257" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11739"/><hi type="bold">35. they shall say--</hi>The heathen, who once made Israel's desolation a ground of reproach against the name of Jehovah Himself (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.20">Eze 36:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.21">21</reference>); but now He so vindicates its sanctity (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.22">Eze 36:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.23">23</reference>) that these same heathen are constrained to acknowledge Israel's more than renewed blessedness to be God's own work, and a ground for glorifying His name (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.36">Eze 36:36</reference>).<div eID="gen21257" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21258" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Eden--</hi>as Tyre (the type of the world powers in general: so Assyria, a cedar "in the garden of God, Eden," <reference osisRef="Ezek.31.8">Eze 31:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.31.9">9</reference>), in original advantages, had been compared to "Eden, the garden of God" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.28.13">Eze 28:13</reference>), from which she had fallen irrecoverably; so Israel, once desolate, is to be as "the garden of Eden" (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.3">Is 51:3</reference>), and is to be so unchangeably. <div eID="gen21258" type="x-p"/>

I will yet for this be inquired of--</hi>so as to grant it. On former occasions He had refused to be inquired of by Israel because the inquirers were not in a fit condition of mind to receive a blessing (<reference osisRef="Ezek.14.3">Eze 14:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.3">20:3</reference>). But hereafter, as in the restoration from Babylon (<reference osisRef="Neh.8.1-Neh.9.38">Ne 8:1-9:38</reference>; Da 9:3-20, 21, 23), God will prepare His people's hearts (<reference osisRef="Ezek.36.26">Eze 36:26</reference>) to pray aright for the blessings which He is about to give (Psa 102:13-17, 20; Zec 12:10-14; 13:<reference osisRef="1Cor.14.1">1</reference>).<div eID="gen21260" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21261" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">like a flock--</hi>resuming the image (<reference osisRef="Ezek.34.23">Eze 34:23</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.34.31">31</reference>). <div eID="gen21261" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 37. I will yet for this be inquired of-- so as to grant it. On former occasions He had refused to be inquired of by Israel because the inquirers were not in a fit condition of mind to receive a blessing ( Eze 14:3 ; 20:3 ). But hereafter, as in the restoration from Babylon ( Ne 8:1-9:38 ; Da 9:3-20, 21, 23), God will prepare His people's hearts ( Eze 36:26 ) to pray aright for the blessings which He is about to give (Psa 102:13-17, 20; Zec 12:10-14; 13: 1 ). like a flock-- resuming the image ( Eze 34:23 , 31 ).
